title: Money received on a partly paid fridge order counts as revenue.
notes: When a customer pays only part of a basket (fridge 0.70.13: the card allowed less, and nobody tapped for the rest), what was paid now appears in sales, analytics and the daily accounting, at the amount actually received.
It is spread over the basket's lines in proportion to their value, so the VSK split (11% / 24%) of what was received matches the basket. Item counts are unchanged: every item did leave the machine.
Such an order is marked partially_paid. If the customer does pay the rest, it becomes an ordinary charged order at the full amount.
The unpaid part is still raised as an alert; it is not booked anywhere.
check: After a partly paid test on 715: the order shows in recent sales at the amount paid (e.g. 8,000 kr), and that day's accounting summary includes it.

title: Unpaid balances on fridge orders are recorded and alerted.
notes: Fridge 0.70.13 reports how much of a basket it collected. When a customer walks away owing money, the order keeps the shortfall and AG gets a critical alert "X kr unpaid" with the order, the amount collected and Nayax's references.
No alert while the kiosk is still asking for the second tap; only when it gives up.
Orders from older apps are recorded exactly as before.

title: A basket over the card's limit is charged up to the limit, then asks for another tap.
notes: Until now a basket that cost more than the card allows in one go (8,000 kr on 715) was refused whole: nothing was charged, Nayax showed "Cancelled by machine", and the screen said it would be charged later, which never happened.

Now the app never asks for more than the reader says the card allows. It charges up to that limit at once, then shows "aðeins X kr. voru gjaldfærðar — vinsamlegast snertu kortið aftur fyrir eftirstöðvunum" with the amount left. The door stays locked; the next tap pays the rest (repeated if the rest is also over the limit).
If nobody taps within 60 seconds, the screen returns to idle and the backend gets the order with what was paid and what is owed.
A refused charge is the same case with nothing paid: "greiðslan fór ekki í gegn" and a tap for the full amount. The old "will be charged when we are back online" screen is gone.
No single charge is ever above 32,767 kr, which the reader could not carry.
check: On 715, then 617: take more than 8,000 kr. Expect 8,000 kr charged at once, the remaining-balance screen, and the rest charged on the second tap — two transactions in Nayax Core. Then repeat without the second tap: one 8,000 kr transaction, and an "unpaid" alert on the dashboard after a minute.

title: Restocking: pressing "open door" again works, and an untouched restock ends in 4 minutes.
notes: Pressing "open door" while the screen already says restocking now sends the unlock again. Before, the press was ignored while the dashboard said "unlocked" (Lava Show, 5 Nov: three presses at the door, none of them did anything). A press for the other cabinet is refused, and the dashboard says so.
While a restock is open the app asks the lock for its state every 15 seconds instead of only listening, so a missed "locked" report no longer leaves the screen on restocking for 10 minutes.

A restock where no basket changes within 4 minutes of the unlock (the 2-minute hold plus 2 minutes) goes back to selling by itself and is not recorded as a restock. A restock with real work still lasts as long as the scales keep moving, up to the hour.
Each unlock only counts when the lock confirms it after that press; an old "unlocked" from an earlier restock is no longer taken as proof.
A door closed with nothing moved is no longer recorded as a restock, so "sold since last restock" is not reset by it.
check: On Lava Show (8626020714): press open door A, wait 3 minutes without opening, press again — the door opens and the log says "open pressed again … sending the unlock again". Leave a restock untouched: it ends after 4 minutes with "the door was not opened in time".

title: An item put back in the wrong basket is caught while the door is open.
notes: Before this, moving an item from one basket to another did nothing on screen: the customer was charged for it (correct, they took it from its basket) and the basket it landed in silently carried the wrong weight, so the next customer to lift it out would be charged for that basket's product. Seen at the trade show, 2026-11-05.

Now, while the door is open, a basket that gets heavier by about the weight of something taken from another basket shows a banner above the cart: „<product>“ er í röngu hólfi — Settu vöruna aftur þar sem þú tókst hana — annars greiðir þú fyrir hana (en/pl too). The item's tile gets a ring and an "í röngu hólfi" badge. Put it back where it came from and both go away and the item leaves the cart.
The charge is never changed by this. If the door closes with the item still in the wrong basket, the customer pays for it as before, and the settlement tells the backend which basket now holds it.
Weight added that matches nothing taken (a bag, a hand) shows nothing to the customer; it is only noted on the settlement.
check: On canary 62160480 (or a show fridge): open, take an item, put it in a different basket. Within a few seconds the banner appears and the tile is marked; put it back and both clear. Close with it still in the wrong basket: the alert "Item in the wrong basket" appears on the dashboard.

title: Fridge sessions show items left in the wrong basket, with an alert to move them back.
notes: A fridge settlement from 0.70.11+ that ends with an item in another basket raises a warning alert, "Item in the wrong basket", for the operator: which basket, how many grams, which product it is and where it came from. Resolving the alert is the "moved it back" step.
The machine page's recent sessions mark such a session "misplaced item" and say what to move where, and what the next customer would otherwise be charged for. The charge itself is untouched.
check: After a test session on the canary that ends with an item in the wrong basket: the alert is on the dashboard and the session row on the machine page carries the note.

title: A machine on a network cable, or behind Tailscale, can be set up and shows as online.
notes: The app only counted Wi-Fi and mobile data as a connection. On a network cable (or when Tailscale's VPN sat in front of a link it didn't name) it showed "ekkert net", and the setup screen refused to even try pairing — "Engin internettenging" while the machine was plainly online. Found setting up a coil machine at the trade show, 2026-11-05.
Any link Android says reaches the internet now counts. The status corner shows "LAN" for it; diagnostics says "snúra / vpn".
check: On a machine with a network cable plugged in: the corner shows LAN, not ekkert net.

notes: Every colour, typeface and corner on the fridge screens now comes from the skin chosen in the dashboard (machine → Controls → Skin, or the operator's default), the same switch as the coil app. Classic is the look so far and the default; nothing changes unless AG switches a machine.

Franklin is the first step of the 2026 redesign: white page, black type and rules, Libre Franklin, square corners. Layouts, the step strip, the cabinet drawing and all timers are unchanged in this build; the redesign of each screen follows behind the same switch.
check: On a canary fridge set Skin = Franklin: within two minutes the idle screen turns white with black type. Set it back to Classic: the cream look returns.

title: Skin switch notes the fridge build.
notes: The Skin control on the machine page now says it applies to fridge 0.70.10 and newer as well as coil 0.80.22.

title: Portrait posters play full screen while the machine is idle.
notes: A poster that is taller than wide (1080×1920 for the 55" screen) now plays full screen when nobody has touched the machine for the idle time, each for its own duration, then round again. A touch anywhere goes straight to the shop.
Upload them in the dashboard like any poster: machine → Screen posters. The upload will say the image is not 16:9; that is expected for these.
Landscape posters and videos keep playing in the strip above the products, as before. Portrait ones never appear there.
When a machine has portrait posters, they are its idle screen; deal cards show on machines without them, as before.
Shown from the copy kept on the machine, so nothing streams. The relayed log says "idle → attract (N posters, M deal cards)".
check: On the canary: upload the coil-55-tommu posters to that machine only, wait ~2 min for the config, leave it untouched for the idle time (30 s by default): the posters cycle full screen; a tap opens the shop.

title: Two skins: Classic and Franklin.
notes: Every colour, typeface and corner on the screens now comes from a skin chosen in the dashboard. Classic is the look the fleet has run so far and is the default; nothing changes unless AG switches a machine.

Franklin is the first step of the 2026 redesign: white page, black type and rules, one typeface (Libre Franklin), square corners, no brand line in the status bar. The screen layouts are unchanged in this build; the redesign of each screen follows behind the same switch.
check: On the canary set Skin = Franklin: within two minutes the grid turns white with black type and square tiles. Set it back to Classic: the cream look returns. Prices and the reader states must stay readable in both.

title: Skins: pick the look a kiosk draws.
notes: AG can set a skin per operator (operator settings) and override it per machine (machine → Controls → Skin). Two exist: Classic, the cream look so far, and Franklin, the 2026 redesign. The machine applies it within two minutes, no restart; coil 0.80.22 or newer.

title: The complaint form returns to idle by itself.
notes: A complaint form opened from the receipt and left alone stayed on screen with a keyboard until someone found "hætta við". It now returns to the idle screen after 60 seconds without a tap or a keystroke; every edit restarts the clock and sending cancels it.
check: After a sale, tap "var eitthvað rangt?" and wait 60 s; the idle screen must come back. Type slowly for over a minute; it must stay.

title: Polish on every customer screen.
notes: Polish was only on the PIN pad; a Polish customer saw Icelandic everywhere else. The whole customer table is now in Polish, and the loading and error screens, which were Icelandic only, follow the chosen language too.
No change for Icelandic or English.
check: Cycle the language pill to PL: the grid, a product page, payment and the success screen must read in Polish.

title: "No sales for N h" now sees sales made through our coil app.
notes: The silent-machine check (Fleet → Health and the 07:45 email) read coil sales from the Weimi order feed only. Sales made through our own coil app were not counted, so both Grótta machines read "no sales for 430 h" while selling every day (137 sales on vinstri since 21 Oct). It now counts completed sales from both sources, once each.
KR, Leiknir and Valur II stay flagged: no sales from them have reached the backend since 17 Oct, because Weimi's order feed now returns nothing for them. That is a separate problem.
Accounting is not changed by this version: the VSK/profit report and the accounting export still miss our coil app's sales.
check: Fleet → Health: Grótta vinstri and hægri no longer show "no sales"; tomorrow's 07:45 email agrees.

title: Code comments: the 502/504 page comes from the edge, probably Cloudflare.
notes: Comments only, no change in behaviour. Three comments said Railway replaces a 502 with its own page. The status-probe test from admin.agvending.is points to Cloudflare in front of Railway instead, so they now say "the edge (probably Cloudflare)".

title: The old features page now sends people to agvending.is/kerfid.
notes: admin.agvending.is/features.html (and /features) answer with a permanent redirect to https://agvending.is/kerfid, the system page on the new company site, which went live on agvending.is today. The page itself is removed.
The link under the dashboard's sign-in box ("Sjá hvað kerfið gerir") goes straight to agvending.is/kerfid.
check: Open admin.agvending.is/features.html: it should land on agvending.is/kerfid.

title: Diagnostic: where a machine's sales come from, and whether accounting sees them.
notes: /api/v1/debug/orders?deviceCode=X&days=14 (AG only, read-only) now splits the machine's sales by source (our kiosk app, Weimi's order feed, fridge settlements). It counts how many kiosk sales have no line in the table the VSK/profit report and the accounting export read, and how many Weimi orders look like the same purchase as a kiosk sale (same total within 3 minutes). Nothing about sales or reports changes in this version; it is there to decide the fix.
check: Open it for a kiosk-run coil machine (e.g. 62160492) and read sources.kioskSalesWithoutOrderItems and sources.weimiOrdersMatchingKioskSales.

title: AG-only test route to find which error codes Railway lets through.
notes: New /api/v1/debug/status-probe?code=503 (AG only). It answers with the status you ask for (400–599) and a fixed JSON body, and does nothing else. If the body arrives, Railway passes that status through and the dashboard can show the backend's own error message. If Railway's page arrives instead, the backend must not use that status for errors (502 is already known to be replaced; upstream failures use 424 since 6.106.3).
check: Run the console snippet for 424, 502, 503 and 504 while signed in as AG: 424 should arrive intact and 502 should not. The result for 503 and 504 decides whether the backend keeps using 503.

title: Orders show how many of a product were bought, not just the line total.
notes: Buying two of the same product is one sale line with a quantity and the line total. The quantity was not kept, so the orders list showed "1 item · Pepsi Max · 1180 kr" for two Pepsi Max at 590 kr, which reads as one drink at 1180 kr (Lava Show, 2026-11-02). The amounts were always right; only the count was missing.
New sales now show "Pepsi Max ×2", and the item count on an order counts units. Top products, the VSK/profit report and the daily accounting summary count units the same way.
Sales recorded before this version have no stored quantity and still read as one unit per line; their amounts are unchanged.
check: After the next multi-unit sale on a coil machine: Activity → view all orders shows the product with ×N and the order says N items.

title: Accounting: a refused send shows Payday's whole answer.
notes: When Payday refused a journal entry, the page said only "HTTP 400": Payday's reason was in a field we did not read. The failure message and the History note now carry Payday's full answer, and the Railway log records the entry that was sent (account IDs and amounts, no login) next to it.
check: Accounting → Send this day now on a day that failed: the red line says what Payday objected to.

title: Accounting: an account is saved the moment it is chosen.
notes: Choosing an account under Accounting → Accounts now saves it at once, and an open preview refreshes with the account names. Before, a chosen account was not stored until Save was pressed further down, so the page looked ready while the send refused with "Choose all three accounts first".
check: Accounting → choose an account: 'Saved' appears under the list, and the preview shows 1110 / 1100 / the clearing account by name.

title: Errors from Payday, Weimi, Nayax and email reach the dashboard instead of "Backend may be restarting".
notes: Every place the backend reported an outside service failing (Payday billing settings, Weimi stock, price, goods and image writes, Nayax, sending emails and replies, the ipify lookup, the Weimi proxy) used HTTP 502. Railway replaces an app's 502 with its own page, so the dashboard showed "Backend may be restarting (HTTP 502)" and the real reason was lost. These now answer 424 with the same message, the way the Accounting connection test has since 6.106.1.
check: Trigger a known upstream failure (e.g. a Weimi write to an offline-for-Weimi machine on Weimi stock, or Billing settings with Payday refusing): the red line names the real error, not "Backend may be restarting".

title: Accounting: diagnose a refused Payday test login.
notes: Spaces, line breaks or quotes around the Railway Payday test login are now ignored.

New AG-only check, /api/v1/debug/accounting-payday-login. It reports whether each test credential is set and how it is shaped (length, whether it looks like a Payday ID, whether it had spaces or quotes), never the value. It also tries signing in to Payday test and Payday live and says which one accepted it.
check: Open /api/v1/debug/accounting-payday-login while signed in as AG: signIn.test should read 'accepted'.

title: Accounting: a failed connection test says what Payday answered.
notes: When Test connection failed, the dashboard said "Backend may be restarting (HTTP 502)" instead of the reason. The backend now answers in a way Railway passes through, so the page shows Payday's own error (sign-in refused, or which call failed and why), and the server log records it as [ACCOUNTING].
check: Accounting → Railway test login → Test connection: either the accounts load, or the red line names Payday's error.

title: Operators can send each day's sales to their own Payday.
notes: New page Business → Accounting (operator admins and AG). An operator picks its accounting system, connects it and chooses three accounts: Nayax clearing, sales 11% and sales 24%.

Each morning from 06:00 the previous day goes over as one journal entry: sales including VAT, with their VAT type (Payday splits the VAT out itself), against the clearing account. Entries are drafts by default, so the bookkeeper posts them.
Payday is the first system. DK, Konto and Business Central are listed as coming.

Nothing is sent until an operator switches it on, and it never goes back before the first day chosen. A day goes over once. If its sales change later, the history shows the difference and a person sends it: an unposted draft is replaced, a posted entry gets a correction for the difference only.
A day that sold a product with no VAT rate is held, not guessed at. Lines the machine did not dispense are not counted as sales, the same rule as the reports.
Preview any day before sending. Logins are stored encrypted and never shown again. If a send times out, it is not retried by itself, since the entry may already be in Payday.
AG can point an operator at the Payday test company with the Railway test login (PAYDAY_CLIENT_ID_TEST / _SECRET_TEST), without pasting anything into the dashboard.
check: Accounting → choose an operator → Payday → Login: Railway test login → Test connection: the test company's accounts load. Map the three accounts, preview yesterday, press 'Send this day now', and find the draft in Payday's test company under unposted journal entries.

title: The daily machine email has the dashboard's look.
notes: The morning machine email now looks like the dashboard: light grey background, white rows, the machine name in heavy black type, small mono section labels, and colour only on the status tags (pink for act now, beige for running low).
Alerts come first, then sold out, then running low. Each product sits on its own row with its slot and how many are left.
Same content and the same Icelandic subject as before; only the look changed. The plain-text version is unchanged.
check: Tomorrow's morning email from a machine with notifications on, in Gmail and on a phone: grey background, white rows, pink and beige tags.

title: The daily machine email has an Icelandic subject line.
notes: The morning machine email's subject now reads e.g. "Íþróttahús — 1 uppselt, 2 að klárast" or "… — 3 vörur að klárast", instead of "1 sold out, 2 low". The body was already Icelandic.
A sold-out count with nothing else running low no longer says ", 0 low".
check: The next morning email from a machine with notifications on: the subject is in Icelandic.

title: The relayed log no longer drops a line at every batch.
notes: The coil app read its log the same way as the fridge app before 0.70.8 and lost lines the same way: roughly one per 5-minute batch, where each batch began, with "--------- beginning of main" in every batch.

The app now reads from just before the last line it sent, by time, so nothing in between can be skipped. If the device's own log has already moved past it, the batch says so with a warning line instead of leaving a silent gap.
A busy five minutes (a restock, a burst of motor errors) is sent in several posts instead of being cut to the newest 400 lines.
Same code as the fridge app now (shared LogCursor), so the two cannot drift apart again.
check: On the canary, machine page → logs: no "beginning of main" lines, and the ProxyClient/VendingViewModel config lines arrive at their usual rhythm with no gap where one batch ends and the next begins.

title: Reports and orders in Icelandic; the public screenshots retaken in Icelandic.
notes: The Reports page (Skýrslur) is now fully Icelandic: the summary tiles, VSK og hagnaður, the VSK breakdown, profit by product, top and slow products, revenue by machine and export. It was mostly English before.
The order list says 'tókst / mistókst / endurgreitt', 'vara / vörur' and 'Nayax-kort', and the field labels on the phone layout are Icelandic too.
The eight screenshots on the features page (and agvending.is/kerfid) are retaken in Icelandic, from an operator's view, on invented demo data.
New tools/demo-data.js fills an empty database with that demo data, so the screenshots can be retaken without touching the real fleet.
check: Switch the dashboard to IS and open Rekstur → Skýrslur and Afgreiðslur: no English left on either page.

title: Demo requests are only confirmed once the email has gone out.
notes: The demo form (now on agvending.is/kerfid, and still on the features page here) is told it went through only after SendGrid has accepted the mail. A failed send shows the email-us fallback instead of a thank-you, so no request is lost silently.
Replying to a demo-request email now answers the person who asked.
check: Send the demo form on agvending.siggip.workers.dev/kerfid with your own address: the mail arrives, and Reply goes to you.

title: agvending.is enquiries say which machine the customer wants.
notes: The contact form on agvending.is has a machine-type list. The choice is in the enquiry email (a "Tæki" line) and at the end of its subject. It is optional; an enquiry without it reads "Tæki: -".
check: Send the form on agvending.siggip.workers.dev with a machine chosen: the subject ends with it and the email has a Tæki line.

title: The agvending.is contact form now reaches you.
notes: New public endpoint POST /api/v1/site-enquiry for the contact form on agvending.is. Each enquiry is emailed as plain text to agvending@agvending.is (SITE_ENQUIRY_TO overrides it), with the customer as reply-to, so answering the email answers them.
The site is told it went through only once SendGrid has accepted the mail. If sending fails, the site shows its email-us fallback instead of the thank-you page, so no enquiry is lost silently.
Honeypot field, and the same rate limit as the demo form: 3 an hour per address, 30 an hour in total.
check: Send the form on agvending.siggip.workers.dev with your own address: the mail arrives at agvending@agvending.is, and Reply goes to you.

title: The relayed log no longer drops a line at every batch.
notes: On Blue Hotel (8626020716) about one line per 5-minute batch never reached the dashboard, always where a batch began: a "config poll: no change" every five minutes, and the update check's outcome at 00:03, 00:33 and 01:03.

Cause: the app read the last 400 lines of its log, and those 400 were counted before the quiet lines (tray weights, poll timing, payment frames) were filtered out. The app writes more than that in five minutes, so the read no longer reached back to where the previous batch ended and the lines in between were skipped.

The app now reads from just before the last line it sent, by time, so nothing in between can be skipped. If the device's own log has already moved past it, the batch says so with a warning line instead of leaving a silent gap.
The "--------- beginning of main" line no longer appears in the relayed log; it was the sign of the problem, not a log line.
A busy five minutes is sent in several posts instead of being cut to the newest 400 lines.
check: On the canary, machine page → logs: "config poll: no change" once a minute with no gaps, OtaScheduler every 30 minutes, and no "beginning of main" lines.

title: A customer screen nobody is using no longer locks out remote commands.
notes: Blue Hotel (8626020716) sat on a customer screen for hours with nobody at the machine, and every dashboard command waited behind it, restart app included.
A screen that has not changed for 15 minutes now counts as stuck: dashboard commands run again, so restart app gets through.
A stuck screen that comes after the payment (receipt, complaint form, declined) returns to idle by itself. A screen during one (authorising, door open, settling) is only logged, never reset.
A charge result that arrives after the receipt timer has run out no longer puts the receipt back on screen without a timer.
The relayed log says which screen is holding commands back and for how long, and logs "STUCK on …" when the 15 minutes pass.
check: Publish to 8626020716 first (once someone has cleared its screen). Normal sales are unchanged; the log line for a deferred command now names the screen.

title: Tailscale comes back after a restart.
notes: The app makes Tailscale the tablet's always-on VPN at every start, so Android starts it after a restart or a power cut. Before, Tailscale stayed off until someone opened it at the machine, and remote adb was out of reach (8626020606, Gym800).

As Device Owner this takes effect at once, so a machine whose Tailscale is signed in but stopped comes back without a visit. Without Device Owner it needs the adb permission grant, and takes effect at the next restart.
Not lockdown: when Tailscale is down the machine still reaches the backend and keeps selling. A different always-on VPN that is already set is left alone.
check: Publish to 8626020606 first. Within a few minutes of the update, adb status should list a 100.x address, and adb connect to 100.119.126.13:5555 should answer.

title: Fridges no longer read "key unknown".
notes: A fridge machine page now says "key stored". Fridges have kept their key on the machine since fridge 0.46.2, and they have no config_health command, so "key unknown" could never change there.
The key-migration banner on the machine list counts coil machines only.
check: Open a fridge (e.g. 8626020606): the header reads "key stored". A coil machine never asked still reads "key unknown".

title: Layer labels come from Weimi, not a guess.
notes: A coil machine's layout now labels each layer spiral or direct-push from Weimi's own slot data. Before, it guessed: top 4 layers spiral, everything below direct-push. That put the wrong label on the bottom layers of six-layer all-coil machines.
A label you set by hand still wins. Tapping a layer now saves only that layer; before, every other layer's guess was saved along with it.
Where a hand-set label disagrees with Weimi, the layer shows "Weimi says …" in red. That means either the label or Weimi's own setup is out of date.
Weimi's type is read at the next sync. Until then a layer reads spiral.
The label is still display only. Charging follows the direct-push rows set on the machine, shown in its health line.
check: After the next Weimi sync, open Stjarnan or Laugardagshöll: their two direct-push layers should read direct-push without anyone setting them.

title: The machine page shows which layers the machine itself treats as direct-push.
notes: A coil machine's direct-push layers are set at the machine (vélbúnaðarpróf → beinar raðir). On those layers a motor that turns less than one turn still counts as a sale. The spiral / direct-push label on the layout is only a label, and nothing on the machine reads it.
The health check now records the machine's setting, and the machine page shows it. If any layer is direct-push on the machine, a warning says which, and how to clear it if those layers are coils.
check: On 62160492 run config_health: the health line must read "direct-push on machine: none" for an all-coil machine.

title: Test vend shows its result where you pressed it.
notes: After a test vend the dashboard waits for the machine and shows the outcome in a message: "motor turned ✓" with the board's code, or what went wrong.
No need to open command history. If a machine on an older app has not answered within 30 seconds, the message says so.
check: Test vend a coil on 62160492: the result message must appear within a few seconds.

title: Dashboard commands run within 5 seconds.
notes: The machine now checks for dashboard commands every 5 seconds, the same as the fridges. Before, it checked only every 2 minutes, so a test vend could wait up to 2 minutes before the motor turned.
Applies to every command (restart, health check, adb, test vend…), not only test vend.
check: On the canary, test vend a coil from the dashboard: the motor should turn within about 5 seconds.

title: Test vend is in the slot menu.
notes: Tapping a coil in the machine's bays & layout now offers Test vend directly, next to Set stock and Set price. No need to open the restock sheet.
It works on empty coils too, to check a motor turns.
check: On 62160492, tap a coil → Test vend → confirm; the result appears in command history.

title: Test vend works on a bay that is on sale.
notes: Every bay in the restock sheet now has a test vend link, not only closed ones. You no longer have to stop selling a coil to test its motor.
The confirmation warns that an item drops if the coil holds product, and that the stock count is not changed: the tester puts the item back. Only if it is kept, press − on that row.
A coil machine below app 0.80.18 still needs the bay closed first; the dashboard says so straight away instead of a failed command minutes later.
check: On the canary, press test vend on an on-sale bay: command history must show the board's result with "on sale" in the detail.

title: Motor test without closing the coil.
notes: A test vend from the dashboard now runs on a coil that is on sale. That coil is taken off the screen only while its motor turns (up to 8 seconds), then comes back by itself.
It is still refused while a customer has something in the basket or is paying; send it again when the machine is idle.
A coil the operator closed stays closed after the test, as before.
check: On the canary, test-vend an on-sale coil: its product disappears from the screen for a few seconds and comes back; command history shows the result code.

title: Stock is counted per coil, for the coil that actually vended.
notes: Config now sends coil machines on Kiosk stock the count in each coil, not only the total per product.
A sale that names its coil (coil app 0.80.17+) is taken off that coil. Older apps' sales are taken off the product's coils in layout order, as before.
check: After a sale on the canary, Bays must show the count drop on the coil that turned (the one in Activity's coil column).

title: A product in several coils vends from one that still has stock.
notes: Until now every unit of a product came out of its first coil. Once that coil was empty the spiral turned with nothing in it and the customer was still charged (Powerade blár, slot 41, while 42–49 were full).
Each unit now comes out of the product's coil with the most left. Two of the same item can come from two coils.
Closing one coil no longer takes the whole product off sale: it stays on sale while any of its coils is open.
Needs backend 6.94.0 for the per-coil counts. On Weimi stock it uses Weimi's counts from the last catalog load.
check: On the canary, buy a product that sits in several coils where the first is empty; it must come out of a full coil, and Activity must show that coil.

title: Activity shows which coil vended each purchase.
notes: On a coil machine's Activity tab, recent orders have a "coil" column (e.g. A35), and each line in an expanded order shows its coil.
Filled from coil app 0.80.16 on; older sales and orders synced from Weimi read "—". Fridges don't show the column.
check: Open the canary's Activity tab after a sale on 0.80.16; the order's coil must match the one that turned.

title: Each sale reports the coil it came out of.
notes: The sale the machine sends to the backend now names the coil each line was vended from, so the dashboard's Activity tab can show it per purchase. Nothing changes on the screen or in payment.
check: Buy one item; Activity → recent orders must show that item's coil (needs backend 6.93.0).

title: The complaint form returns to the grid by itself.
notes: Twice in one afternoon a customer opened the complaint form from the success screen and walked away, leaving the machine on a form with a keyboard for ten minutes and more. It now goes back to the grid after 60 seconds without a touch or a keystroke, as "Hætta við" does; never while a complaint is being sent.
check: After a sale, open the complaint form and wait 60 s; the grid must come back. Type slowly for over a minute; it must stay.

title: Product info returns to the grid by itself.
notes: A product's info page left open used to stay until the next tap: nothing timed it out unless deal cards were configured. It now goes back to the grid after 30 seconds without a touch; the basket is kept, as with "Til baka".
check: Open a product's info page and wait 30 s without touching; the grid must come back.

title: The blank cream screen is fixed.
notes: Two quick taps on "Til baka" could empty the screen and leave the machine deaf while the dashboard said online. Every back now lands on the grid, and the app goes home by itself if the screen ever empties.
The screen watchdog restarts the app on any flat, single-colour screen, not only a black one.
check: Tap "Til baka" twice fast on a product page; the grid must stay.

title: Idle guard, per machine.
notes: A switch under Controls (AG only) keeps one CPU core out of the deep sleep that stopped Grótta vinstri for 44 minutes twice in one night. Off unless switched on; measured on one machine first.

title: A failed update download is retried.
notes: One download that failed used to block that build until the app restarted; hægri sat on an old build that way. A failed download now retries at the next hourly check.

title: Header never mixes versions.
notes: The log relay carries the build code, so the dashboard header cannot pair a new version name with the old build's number.

title: The machine says why an update is withheld.
notes: "útgáfa í bið" now names the reason: not in the release group, rollout halted, or the machine still needs pairing for its own key.
The version name reaches the dashboard header with every update check.

title: Wireless debugging from the dashboard.
notes: "adb on / status / off" on the machine page (AG only); the answer carries the connect line, so nobody has to read the screen.

title: Out of service works on coil.
notes: The dashboard switch covers the screen with "Lokað tímabundið" and the operator's reason; a payment already running finishes first. The clock long-press still reaches the PIN pad.

title: Each machine gets its own admin PIN.
notes: The PIN pad checks the machine's own PIN from the dashboard (machine → admin PIN); no PIN set means the shared code still works.
Five wrong tries lock the pad for five minutes, kept across restarts, and raise an alert.

title: Shared module with the fridge app.
notes: Self-healing, auto-revert, the installer, the clock guard, the screen watchdog and the card-reader report are now one copy for both apps. No change in behaviour on the machine.

title: Card reader in the header.
notes: The machine reports its Nayax reader (serial, firmware) and whether the card link is up; the header shows the serial instead of "Nayax —", and a dead link raises an alert.

title: Updates check even on a SIM router.
notes: The hourly update check ran only on networks Android calls unmetered, which the SIM router is not; it now runs regardless, five minutes after start and hourly after, and logs the outcome.
The dashboard's check-update command works on coil machines.

title: Dead screens restart; ads from the backend.
notes: A watchdog restarts the app when the screen stops drawing or stays black.
The ad region plays the list set in the dashboard, from a local copy; nothing streams over the SIM any more.
The app relays its log to the dashboard (machine → logs).

title: First build released by CI.
notes: No change on the machine; this build proved the release pipeline end to end.

title: The clock stays right.
notes: The setup and error screens say "klukkan í vélinni er röng" when the clock is years off, and the app switches automatic time back on at every start.

title: Set up by pairing code.
notes: A six-digit code from the dashboard hands the machine its own key. No more keys baked into builds.

title: Idle guard, per machine.
notes: Same switch as on coil (Controls, AG only): keeps one CPU core out of deep sleep. Off unless switched on.

title: A failed update download is retried.
notes: A failed download no longer blocks that build until the next restart; it retries at the next check.

title: Header never mixes versions.
notes: The log relay carries the build code, so the header cannot pair a new name with an old number.

title: Update reasons in words.
notes: The update log says why a build is withheld (not in the release group, halted, key not stored). The version name reaches the header with every check.

title: Wireless debugging from the dashboard.
notes: "adb on / status / off" on the machine page (AG only), from fridge 0.70.0. From this build the fridge app lives in the same repository as the coil app and shares code with it.

title: Admin PIN code shared with coil.
notes: No change on the machine; the PIN code moved to the shared module.

title: Automatic time kept on.
notes: The app switches automatic time back on at every start, as the coil app does. A wrong clock after a power cut fails every connection while the screen looks fine.
Self-healing, auto-revert and the installer are now shared with the coil app.

title: What's new, on the dashboard.
notes: This row. One entry per version of the coil app, the fridge app and the backend, newest first, with how many machines run each build.

title: The dashboard can be translated.
